newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Downtrodden Aussie has date with year low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Downtrodden Aussie has date with year low.

text.p: *AUD looking vulnerable after failing to sustain even a modest bounce from 76 cents in face of NY bank and option sales
*Flows two-way as exporters on the bid, but sentiment bearish on yield differentials and 1997 low of $0.7550 at risk *Even CRB index turned against AUD with a 3.0 point plunge
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the dollar was pinned at US$0.7599/04 having crept as high as US$0.7632 offshore following Friday's local 3/4 cent plunge to US$0.7604/09.

Bears were aiming for US$0.7550, the trough reached on February 12 when the dollar was still reeling from the December rate cut which, like the one two weeks ago, came as a surprise to much of the market.
A breach there would return the currency to levels not seen since February 1996 and risk a lapse to the 73 cent low reached in January of that year.
On the crosses the A$ was a sideshow to the Euro-currencies.

The market was struggling with the implications of a win by the left wing in the French elections. The blow was all the greater as seat projections suggested the Socialists would need the support of the Communists to rule.

Both parties had reservations about EMU, leading the market to fear the result would be a softer single currency. That had bearish implications for the mark's hard-won credibility and the German currency dipped against both dollars this morning.
On the domestic front the Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting Tuesday, ensuring some tension Wednesday morning, but few believe it will move so soon after the last easing.
Nevertheless, another cut was a possibility down the track if the run of economic data were anything like as soft as the 1.7 percent dive in April retail trade.
Today's April building approvals data should at least show the housing recovery remains underway, albeit slowly. Forecasts favour a 3.0 percent rise after a 1.8 percent drop in March.

March quarter GDP figures are due Thursday and most analysts have been revising down their forecasts following a surprise fall in inventories reported last week. Median estimates are for a 0.8 percent rise on the quarter which would see annual growth slow to 2.2 percent from 3.1. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
